fields.meta_title: Free Club Sign Up Sheet Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a club sign up sheet that fills every club roster from one QR code and closes a club when its spots run out. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Club Sign-Up Sheet That Fills Every Roster
fields.hero_description: Make a club sign up sheet that puts each student on the right club roster and emails them the first meeting time.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After a Student Signs Up
fields.features_subheading: A printed grid ends the fair as a page of handwriting to retype. Each part below acts on a sign-up the moment it arrives.
fields.feature_1:
One QR code for every club at the fair

Print one code for the table banner. A student scans it and ticks the clubs they want, and the name lands on each of those rosters. Nobody retypes a smudged page that evening.
fields.feature_2:
Spots that close at the number you set

Give any club a cap, such as 24 for a chess club with 12 boards. Once the cap is reached, that club drops off the list, and later sign-ups can join a waitlist instead.
fields.feature_3:
Questions that change with the club

Ask drama sign-ups whether they want to act or work on the crew. Ask debate sign-ups which events they want to try. A student sees only the questions for the clubs they picked.
fields.feature_4:
A welcome email with the first meeting

The app emails each new member the meeting day and room as soon as they sign up. A second email goes out the day before the first meeting, with the advisor's name on it.
fields.feature_5:
A roster page for each advisor

Each advisor opens a page with only their own club's members, plus a grade and a school email beside each name. Every sign-up from every club sits in one database you own.
fields.feature_6:
No limit on how many students sign up

Emergent puts no cap on responses, and a fair that brings in 400 names keeps the form open to the last student in line. The free tier covers building and publishing it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Clubs That Dropped the Clipboard
fields.tab_content_1:
By the bell, all 18 clubs have rosters

Dunmore Park High holds its fall club fair in the gym at lunch, with one QR code on the banner at the door. Students tick as many of the 18 clubs as they like. By the bell, 214 students have signed up, and robotics advisor Henrike Ofori opens a roster of 31 names.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every audition slot goes to one actor

Pell Hollow Middle School's drama club starts its sheet with one question: act or crew. Crew sign-ups skip ahead. Students who want to act pick one of 9 ten-minute audition slots on Tuesday after school. Wrenna Calloway books 4:10 pm, and that slot disappears for everyone after her.
fields.tab_content_3:
After 12 readers, the sheet starts a waitlist

Wickham Lane Readers meets in a member's living room, which seats 12. Each reader who signs up picks a month to host. Corwin Ashdale is the 13th to sign up. He goes on the waitlist at number 1 and gets an email with his place in line.
fields.tab_content_4:
With 4 parents in, the shift drops off

The Cobalt Creek High band boosters run the concession stand at 5 home games, 2 shifts a game. Each shift needs 4 parents and drops off the sheet once it has them. Adaeze Holloway took Friday at 6:00 pm, and on Thursday evening she gets an email about her shift.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Club Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to make a club sign up sheet that sends every student to the right club roster.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every club and its advisor
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set caps where space runs out
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each club with its advisor and its meeting room. These details fill the roster pages and the welcome email, and they are far easier to gather before the fair than after it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask every student for a name and a school email, plus a grade if clubs are split by year. Anything only one club needs belongs in that club's own questions.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a question only when the person running the club will use the answer, such as an instrument for jazz band or a portfolio link for an art club. Each one shows only to students who tick that club.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give a club a cap only when something limits it, such as seats or easels. Decide whether students past the cap join a waitlist or see the club marked full.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your club list into one prompt and say what each club asks and where its cap sits. Emergent builds the sheet and the advisor rosters, and you change either by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with a few students
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask 3 students to sign up on their own phones before the fair. Check that each name lands on the right rosters and that a full club closes when it should.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Print the code big enough to scan from a step away, and tape a copy to each club table. Share the link in the school newsletter for anyone who misses the fair.

faq_plan.q: What is a club sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: A club sign up sheet is a list where people put their names down to join a club. It also asks for whatever the organizer needs to reach them, such as an email or a grade. At a school club fair, students add their names to each club they want to try. An online version files each name onto the right club's roster as it arrives.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a club sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Start with two lists: the clubs, and the questions every student answers. Describe both in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, along with any club that caps its members, and Emergent builds the sheet and a roster for each advisor. A typed copy of your old paper sheet is enough to start the prompt, and you can change the result by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Should a drama club sign up sheet ask about rehearsal conflicts?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask which weekday afternoons the student cannot stay after school, plus any known dates away, such as a family trip in March. The director can then plan rehearsals around real conflicts before casting, not after it.

faq_plan.q: Is a club sign up sheet template enough, or should I build my own?
faq_plan.a: A template is enough when one club needs a list of names on paper. Build your own once several clubs share a sheet or a club has a cap on members. The same choice comes up with a potluck sign up sheet, where a printed grid suits a small dinner and falls short once each course has slots that close.

faq_plan.q: How do I use a book club sign up sheet to rotate hosts?
faq_plan.a: Add a month picker and let each reader claim one month to host. Remove a month from the choices once it is taken, and the year's schedule builds itself as people sign up. Emergent can build a reminder email to each host a week before their month into the same app.

faq_plan.q: How many students should an art club sign up sheet allow?
faq_plan.a: Set the cap from the room, not a round number. Count the seats at the art room tables, or the easels if members paint standing up, and stop the sheet there. If a club shares one kiln or one printing press, plan around how many pieces it takes in a session.

faq_plan.q: What fields belong on a book club sign up sheet template?
faq_plan.ref: book club sign up sheet template
faq_plan.secondary: book club sign up sheet template
faq_plan.a: Ask for a name and an email, plus a phone number for last-minute venue changes. Add a line for book suggestions if the group votes on titles, and a note field for anyone who reads in audio or large print. If the club grows into a public author event with sessions and badges, a conference registration form fits that better.

faq_plan.q: How should I set up volunteer shifts on a booster club sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Make each shift its own slot with a set number of parents, and show the open count beside it, such as 2 of 4. A week before game day, email the whole parent list with only the shifts still open. The app Emergent builds can send that email from the same sheet, with no cap on how many parents sign up.

faq_plan.q: What should a chess club sign up sheet ask about experience?
faq_plan.a: Ask how long the student has played and whether they have a rating, with none as a valid answer. The advisor can then pair new players with each other for the first few weeks instead of matching them against the club's strongest players.

faq_plan.q: Should a club sign up sheet collect a parent's contact details?
faq_plan.a: For students, yes: ask for a parent or guardian email, and check whether your school's own policy asks for anything more. For adult clubs, the member's own email is enough. A program that runs for weeks with medical and pickup details needs a summer camp registration form instead.
